Paths must be ASCII: both Package.InstalledLocation.Path and ApplicationData.LocalFolder.Path are converted by the narrowing std::string ctor 0x480D8 (low byte of each UTF-16 unit), so a non-ASCII install or profile directory silently corrupts every asset/storage path.

Process cwd is a requirement, not a hedge: D3DCompile (call at 0xD6C94) passes pSourceName = 'data/<name>' (relative) and pInclude = D3D_COMPILE_STANDARD_FILE_INCLUDE ((ID3DInclude*)1, str 1 at [sp] 0xD6C8A) with Flags1 0x8000; the dx11 shaders #include "ShaderConstants.fxh" which sits in data/shaders/dx11, so the include only resolves if the cwd is the folder that contains data\.

Fake WinRT objects need more than the slot list: QueryInterface (slot 0) on the fake IStorageFolder must answer IID 4207A996-CA2F-42F7-BDE8-8B10457A7F30 (IStorageItem); AddRef/Release (slots 1/2) are called on every object; get_Path (slot 12) must return a real HSTRING (the game calls WindowsGetStringRawBuffer/WindowsDeleteString); IPackageStatics.get_Current slot 6, IPackage.get_InstalledLocation slot 7, IApplicationDataStatics.get_Current slot 6, IApplicationData.get_LocalFolder slot 12, IMemoryManagerStatics slots 6/7 return UINT64 (r0:r1); the exe's HIDController ctor (0x1103FC) needs the real vccorlib120_app Platform::Object. The ThreadPool fake must call the handler's COM Invoke at vtable slot 3; the init lambda ignores the IAsyncAction argument while the render-loop body 0x1DA160 dereferences it.

First-screen sizing: Minecraft::init2 (0x1D8558) calls setSize(client+0x20,+0x24,0.0f) with the ctor values 1x1, so StartMenuScreen is built at GUI size 1x1 / guiScale 1 and only fixes itself when the host's setSize runs. The host must call client->vtbl[20](W,H,0.0f) after init and before the first Minecraft::update, and must first write platform+0x38 (ppmm), +0x3C/+0x40 (=1.0f), +0x30/+0x34, otherwise OnWindowSizeChanged-style math produces width 0 and the 240x140 fallback. Writing client+0x20/+0x24 before runInit is also viable because setSize is NULL-safe and init2 re-applies those fields.

World auto-load branch at the end of init was mis-described as a gamepad query: client+0xAC is ExternalFileLevelStorageSource and the branch (0x58278-0x582DA) loads the first world through client vtbl[26] when options[0x290] is set (likely 'dev_autoloadlevel', string 0x227E64); default is 0 (0xA0D54) but a persisted options.txt under <LocalFolder>/games/com.mojang/minecraftpe can change the first screen. The level enumeration uses FindFirstFileExW (plain Win32 files), no WinRT.

Any host-allocated object handed to the game must come from the game's CRT heap: queued input events are freed by pollInputEvent with operator delete (0x4B428 -> thunk 0x20043C); allocate them via thunk 0x200430 (??2@YAPAXI@Z) and match the exact event size/layout from the input area.

Client vtable slots 9,10,11,12,33,34 (sound pass-through to +0x138) and 17/39 (screen vtbl[28]/[29] pass-through) are still unlabeled in the facts; the item/tile registration calls at the end of Minecraft::init2 (0x19B528,0x1CC2C0,0x15A800,0x163384,0x1BACA4) were not decoded and run on every init, so a crash there would not be diagnosable from the facts.

Ordering notes absent from the facts: the MainPage ctor also starts a High-priority TimeSliced ThreadPool job at 0x1DD40E (the CoreIndependentInputSource dispatcher loop, work item 0x1DE0BC, stored at MainPage+0x6C) which is unrelated to the client; AppMain's DR owner (setOwner at 0x1D9D90) is set after the init job is queued - I checked that init never reads DR+0x74 (only Present/HandleDeviceLost do), so a synchronous fake RunAsync is safe.
